#### **Describe how access to traffic generators (businesses, schools, etc.) and everyday services will be maintained:**

Local traffic, including emergency vehicles, school buses, postal delivery, and garbage collection will need to utilize alternate routes available near the closed segment of STH 56 to bypass the closed segment of STH 56. Through traffic will be directed to utilize the signed detour provided to bypass the closed segment of STH 56. No official access points exist within the closed segment of STH 56. Adjacent property owners, local officials and emergency services were notified of the project via mailing and they were asked to respond with any comments or concerns. At this time no comments or concerns have been received.

#### **Are there anticipated traffic impacts from the proposed project on other road/routes in the region/corridor?**

STH 56 traffic will be detoured to STH 82 and STH 131. It is not anticipated that the detoured STH 56 traffic will negatively impact the operations or roadway conditions of STH 82 or STH 131.

#### **Does the project affect other regions/states?**

No

#### **List holidays or major special events that occur during the project:**

| Holiday/Special Event | Begin Date | End Date   |
|-----------------------|------------|------------|
| Memorial Day          | 05/27/2022 | 05/31/2022 |
| Fourth of July        | 07/01/2022 | 07/05/2022 |
| Labor Day             | 09/02/2022 | 09/06/2022 |

#### **How will traffic disruptions be minimized during listed events and holidays?**

The contract documents will contain standard special provisions that prohibit working on and hauling materials along or across any portion of STH 56, STH 82, or STH 131 during these holiday periods. Although the Labor Day Holiday falls outside of the anticipated end date, it has been included since the project is a working day contract and the exact construction dates are unknown and chosen by the contractor. The engineer will have the ability to suspend work activities beyond the periods listed above in the event any undesirable traffic congestion develops that has the potential to cause lengthy motorist delay or unsafe working conditions.

--- End of Section 5 ---

#### **Briefly describe the staging planned for maintaining traffic:** PROJECT 5130-00-80 WILL BE COMPLETED UTILIZING A SINGLE LANE, ONE-WAY TEMPORARY BYPASS STRUCTURE. Stage 2 will construct the permanent STH 71 structure and the left half of the roadway. Traffic will utilize single lane, one-way, bypass structure under temporary signals. Stage 3 will construct the eastbound STH 71 travel lane, lower pavement layer only. Pedestrian access to businesses shall be maintained as much as possible during the project to allow customer and mail access. The closure of W Milwaukee Street between Center Ave and River Street will minimally impact normal transit services. #### **Brief description of work activities:**

The overall project limits are from the west Jackson County line to 300 feet west of USH 12 North. The existing pavement within the project limits will be resurfaced including milling of various depths as specified in the plans at turn lanes, side roads, and beam guard locations, followed by 3.5 inches of cold-in-place recycle (CIR), followed by a 2.75" depth final asphaltic pavement overlay. A HSIP project (1520-02-70) has been approved for completion with this project to help address the frequency of ROR crashes along this segment of highway. The HSIP project will widen the existing 3' paved shoulders to 8' and maintain the total shoulder width of 8'. The wider paved shoulders will provide a wider area for the many buggies that travel this corridor. Center line rumble strips will also be added to warn drivers that they are deviating from their travel lanes into possible on-coming traffic and reduce the risk of head-on collisions. Other repair or incidental work being proposed with the project includes repairing or replacing sections of substandard beam guard to current standards. The beam guard needing adjustments or replacement are located throughout the project corridor at five box culvert or bridge crossings and three steeper sloped embankments. Several of the existing concrete culvert pipes and endwall sections throughout the corridor have experienced separation at the joints and will be repaired by relaying the separated pipe sections and installing new endwalls. The existing culverts will be cleaned and the ditches near the culvert ends will be cleaned within the existing right-of-way to clear brush, debris, and sediment to provide proper drainage. Concrete box culvert C-27-0012 located east of CTH T on the North Fork Buffalo River will have concrete surface repairs completed on the inside of the culvert. All proposed work will take place within the existing right-of-way. The CIR of the existing pavement and the new HMA pavement will be performed while the road is closed to through traffic with the use of a signed detour, with all remaining construction operations being performed while the road is open to through traffic. Although the attached Work Zone Impact Assessment shows the user costs are lower for keeping USH 10 open to traffic with the use of flaggers, the road closed to traffic utilizing a detour was selected in order to limit the amount of time the CIR layer is exposed to traffic and to help protect the CIR shoulders which cannot have traffic run on them until after the HMA pavement is in place. Special Provisions will be included that requires the roadway to be opened to through traffic upon completion of the HMA pavement. The CIR special provisions

require the Contractor to pave the lower layer of the HMA within 5 days of the CIR reaching moisture requirements, which will in turn require the Contractor to complete the lower layer of the HMA in a timely manner. The Special Provisions will require the USH 10 roadway to be opened to through traffic immediately after completing the lower layer of HMA pavement. Although the roadway will be opened to traffic after the HMA lower layer is paved, it is likely the Contractor will begin paving the surface layer while the roadway is closed and soon after the lower layer paving begins to reduce down time since the HMA paving operations are considerable faster than CIR operations.

The overall project limits are from the west Jackson County line to 300 feet west of USH 12 North. The existing pavement within the project limits will be resurfaced including milling of various depths as specified in the plans at turn lanes, side roads, and beam guard locations, followed by 3.5 inches of cold-in-place recycle (CIR), followed by a 2.75" depth final asphaltic pavement overlay. A HSIP project (1520-02-70) has been approved for completion with this project to help address the frequency of ROR crashes along this segment of highway. The HSIP project will widen the existing 3' paved shoulders to 8' and maintain the total shoulder width of 8'. The wider paved shoulders will provide a wider area for the many buggies that travel this corridor. Center line rumble strips will also be added to warn drivers that they are deviating from their travel lanes into possible on-coming traffic and reduce the risk of head-on collisions. Other repair or incidental work being proposed with the project includes repairing or replacing sections of substandard beam guard to current standards. The beam guard needing adjustments or replacement are located throughout the project corridor at five box culvert or bridge crossings and three steeper sloped embankments. Several of the existing concrete culvert pipes and endwall sections throughout the corridor have experienced separation at the joints and will be repaired by relaying the separated pipe sections and installing new endwalls. The existing culverts will be cleaned and the ditches near the culvert ends will be cleaned within the existing right-of-way to clear brush, debris, and sediment to provide proper drainage. Concrete box culvert C-27-0012 located east of CTH T on the North Fork Buffalo River will have concrete surface repairs completed on the inside of the culvert. All proposed work will take place within the existing right-of-way. The CIR of the existing pavement and the new HMA pavement will be performed while the road is closed to through traffic with the use of a signed detour, with all remaining construction operations being performed while the road is open to through traffic. Although the attached Work Zone Impact Assessment shows the user costs are lower for keeping USH 10 open to traffic with the use of flaggers, the road closed to traffic utilizing a detour was selected in order to limit the amount of time the CIR layer is exposed to traffic and to help protect the CIR shoulders which cannot have traffic run on them until after the HMA pavement is in place. Special Provisions will be included that requires the roadway to be opened to through traffic upon completion of the HMA pavement. The CIR special provisions

require the Contractor to pave the lower layer of the HMA within 5 days of the CIR reaching moisture requirements, which will in turn require the Contractor to complete the lower layer of the HMA in a timely manner. The Special Provisions will require the USH 10 roadway to be opened to through traffic immediately after completing the lower layer of HMA pavement. Although the roadway will be opened to traffic after the HMA lower layer is paved, it is likely the Contractor will begin paving the surface layer while the roadway is closed and soon after the lower layer paving begins to reduce down time since the HMA paving operations are considerable faster than CIR operations.

#### **Describe how access to traffic generators (businesses, schools, etc.) and everyday services will be maintained:**

STH 22 will be open to traffic at all times during construction hours. During non-construction hours both lanes of STH 22 will be open to traffic. Businesses, residents, and the school will have access at all times. Replacing the cross culvert at station 486+69 will be done by utilizing a detour. STH 22 will be closed from CTH QQ to CTH K for 5 days (Monday- Friday) to install the pipe. Signage at CTH QQ and CTH K will allow local traffic acess to businesses and residents. STH 22 will be closed at the culvert replacement location. All businesses and residents will have access from either the east or west. The detour will happen after the 4th of July weekend so school will not be in session.

#### **Describe how impacts to bicycle riders will be mitigated/coordinated:**

Temporary curb ramps will be provided on the multi-use path. Bicyclists can use the paved shoulder on STH 22 or a local side road (Western Avenue) which runs parallel to STH 22 between USH 10 and CTH K approximately 450 feet to the north.

#### **Are there anticipated traffic impacts from the proposed project on other road/routes in the region/corridor?**

No. STH 22 will operate as it currently does with full access. Minor delays due to the flagging operation are expected but should not cause motorists to seek other routes or impact other regional corridors. The proposed detour route uses STH 21, STH 49 and US 10. These routes are all under capacity and can handle the additional traffic of the detour.

#### **Does the project affect other regions/states?**

No. This project is very localized in nature.

#### **Describe how access to traffic generators (businesses, schools, etc.) and everyday services will be maintained:**

For each structure location, through traffic will be maintained throughout construction as well as access to all properties adjacent to the project. Minor interruptions are anticipated to occur at the bridge locations that will utilize the "One Lane Road with Temporary Signals" system.

### **Describe how impacts to bicycle riders will be mitigated/coordinated:**

Structure B-68-0124 is the only one of the seven bridges that provides formal bicycle accommodations--the River Ridge Trail located along the southbound side of the bridge. A shuttle service will be provided to assist Bicyclists across the work zone in either direction throughout construction. Structures B-24-0009 and B-68-0071/0100/0101/0130 have approaches that contain paved shoulders, which may be used by bicyclists. For structures B-68-0071 & 0130 where traffic will be controlled by the "One Lane Road with Temporary Signal System", bicyclists may navigate through the construction zone while the signal allows them the right-of-way. For structures B-24-0009, B-68-0100 & 0101 where traffic will be maintained with little to no shoulder, any potential bicyclist would need to find an alternative route, which will not be designated as part of this project. Structure B-68-0117 is located within an urban area with sidewalks on each side of the bridge. Bicyclists have the ability to walk their bike through the construction zone. Alternatively, since traffic will be controlled by the "One Lane Road with Temporary Signal System", bicyclists may navigate through the construction zone while the signal allows them the right-ofway.

#### **Describe how impacts to railways will be mitigated/coordinated:**

Structure B-68-0071 spans a Canadian National rail line. No impacts to the rail line will occur. An at-grade railroad crossing is located approximately 0.3 miles north of structure B-68-0117; however, no impacts to the crossing will occur.

NB | 150 | 6 | 0.17 | Flagging | #### **How was the work zone capacity determined?** The STH 153 work zone capacity under flagging operations was determined using Synchro Traffic Modeling Software. Traffic models were analyzed using construction year (2023) K30 volumes, which were calculated from the design values given in the traffic forecast. This location has an anticipated 2023 AADT of 3,525 with a K30 peak directional volume of 240 veh/hr. The work zone was modeled as a temporary trailer mounted traffic signal with actuated signal timing. Flagging operations will have similar impacts to traffic as the temporary signals would. In some cases the flaggers may be able to prioritize traffic better based on demand. Using K30 volumes, STH 153 traffic is expected to operate at a LOS F due to the introduction of flagging operations and the large delays are due to work zone lengths potentially reaching 1-2 miles in length. See Attachment 5 for the results of the capacity analysis. The proposed detour route includes diverting traffic at the STH 153 & STH 107 intersection and the IH 39 interchange with STH 153 to follow STH 107, STH 29, US 51, and IH 39. The detour will be in place for a total of 12 calendar days. The capacity of the detour route was determined based on information in the Highway Capacity Manual 6th Edition Chapter 15 'Two-Lane Highways' and Chapter 12 ' Basic Freeway and Multilane Highway Segments'. These chapters suggest a capacity of 1,700 vphpl for a rural two-lane highway facility (STH 107), a capacity of 2,300 vphpl for a multilane highway segment with a posted speed of 65 mph (STH 29 and US 51), and a capacity of 2,400 vphpl for a basic freeway segment with a posted speed of 70 mph (IH 39). There will be some additional delay along the off-ramps at the IH 39 interchange with STH 153 and the STH 29 interchange with STH 107 and at multiple intersections along the detour route: STH 153 & CTH B (Signalized), STH 153 & Old Hwy 51/Ranger St. (Roundabout), STH 153 & Old Hwy 51/CTH DB (TWSC), and IH 39 SB off-ramp & STH 153 (Signalized). There are also speed reductions along STH 153 within the City of Mosinee and along STH 107 within the Village of Marathon City. STH 107 has a 2016 AADT of 9,300 (from TCMap) and peak directional volume of 530 vphpl. STH 29 has a 2019 AADT of 26,100 (from TCMap) and peak directional volume of 740 vphpl. US 51 has a 2019 AADT of 65,500 (from TCMap) and peak directional volume of 1,850 vphpl. IH 39 has a 2019 AADT of 39,600 (from TCMap) and peak directional volume of 1,345 vphpl. The K30 peak directional volume for STH 153 is 240 vphpl, based on the traffic forecast. The proposed detour route is expected to operate under capacity when including STH 153 traffic volumes. Note that US 51 and IH 39 have higher than usual SB traffic volumes on Sunday's due to the summer recreational traffic traveling to south Wisconsin/Illinois at the end of the weekends. See Attachment 6 for the detour route hourly volumes. The additional delay and travel distance due to the full closure of STH 153 was determined by using the posted speed limit and distance traveled for the signed detour route. #### **Describe how access to traffic generators (businesses, schools, etc.) and everyday services will be maintained:**

Access will be maintained at all intersections and driveways along STH 97 except at CTH AAA/ Galvin Avenue, Staadt Avenue and Drake Avenue. CTH AAA/Galvin Avenue and Staadt Avenue will be allowed to be temporarily closed for a maximum of 5 working days while the intersection approaches are be reconstructed. CTH AAA/Galvin Avenue and Staadt Avenue will not be allowed to be closed at the same time unless otherwise allowed by the engineer. Drake Avenue will allowed to be temporarily closed during the deck overlay of structure B-37-104. Short term closures will occur while milling and paving operations take place in front of all driveways and other intersections within the project limits. Traffic will be managed with flaggers and coordination will occur with property owners.

#### **Describe how impacts to bicycle riders will be mitigated/coordinated:**

Bikes will be maintained on the travel lanes of STH 97 during construction.

#### **Are there anticipated traffic impacts from the proposed project on other road/routes in the region/corridor?**

During the deck overlay on the bridge over the Little Eau Pleine River, large trucks especially with trailers will be restricted from turning north due to the location of the intersection to the bridge work. Special signing will be required along CTH T to notify travelers of a potential access restriction to STH 97. There are no other anticipated traffic impacts on other roads /routes in the region/corridor.

The project will not affect any other regions or states.

Prior to reopening lanes to traffic, bring the travel surface flush with the existing grade around or adjacent to all manholes, water valves, or curb and gutter with temporary base aggregate, temporary pavement or the permanent pavement surface. Maintain local and emergency traffic on STH 97 at all times. Side Roads Maintain full access to and from STH 97 at all side roads with the use of flagging operations to control traffic as required during work operations within and at the intersections unless otherwise allowed per these special provisions and by the engineer. Construct driveways in stages as required to maintain traffic. Keep all entrances accessible at all times, except for temporary restrictions during the milling and paving operations in the immediate vicinity of the entrance. No extended closures of entrances will be allowed without approval of the engineer and written permission is obtained from the property owner 48 hours in advance of closing the access. If work is being completed on multiple driveways to the same property, conduct operations so at least one of the driveways remain open.

### **Describe how impacts to bicycle riders will be mitigated/coordinated:**

Single lane closures will be utilized during construction. On-road bicycles may use the open lanes of traffic similar to existing conditions.

### **Are there anticipated traffic impacts from the proposed project on other road/routes in the region/corridor?**

No traffic impacts from the proposed project are anticipated on other roads/routes in the region/corridor.

### **Does the project affect other regions/states?**

Parts of WIS 13 within the project limits run along the shared line of Marathon and Clark counties, which is also the border between the North Central and Northwest Regions. There are no conflicts in the bordering Northwest Region associated with the project.

Keep the STH 13 intersections at Spence Street, Adams Street, Elderberry Road, Linden Street, and Spruce Street open at all times. Reduce Spence Street, Adams Street, Elderberry Road, Linden Street, and Spruce Street traffic to one lane utilizing flagging operations when construction operations are within these intersections. Traffic access to STH 13 at all other intersections may be closed when construction operations are within the area. When an intersection is closed, keep the adjacent intersections open to traffic. Maintain one lane of traffic in each direction on STH 13 and all major connecting side roads at all times as shown in the plans and as described below except where one-lane flagging operations are required north of Station 1205+10. Maintain pedestrian traffic throughout the project at all times. Construct the pedestrian curb ramps and sidewalks in stages as shown in the plans and described below. Install temporary sidewalks, temporary curb ramps, and the traffic control for sidewalk and pedestrian crossing closures prior to any work impacting these facilities. Stage construction as follows: Stage 1: Merge STH 13 northbound traffic to the outside through lane south of CTH N. Shift southbound traffic to the outside edge of the roadway north of Pine Street as shown in the plans. Close the northbound and southbound inside through lanes. Construct the inside through lanes between the project beginning and Station 1205+10, all left turn lanes, and center two-way-left-turn lanes within the closure. Construct the new overlay pavement after the pedestrian curb ramps listed under Stages 1-1 and 1-2 are completed. Maintain a minimum 11 foot lane width for both directions of STH 13 at all times. Stage 1-1: Construct the pedestrian curb ramps located in the center median islands as shown in the plans while the inside traffic lanes are closed to through traffic. Stage 1-2: Construct the pedestrian curb ramp located in the center median island as shown in the plans while the inside traffic lanes are closed to through traffic and after the adjacent curb ramp is completed in Stage 1-1 and open to pedestrian cross traffic. Stage 2: Merge STH 13 northbound traffic to the inside through lane south of CTH N. Remove the shift for the southbound traffic placed in stage 1 north of Pine Street and place the southbound traffic back to the center lane. Close the northbound and southbound outside through lanes. Construct the outside through lanes between the project beginning and Station 1205+10, all right turn lanes, and shoulders within the closure. Construct the new overlay pavement after the pedestrian curb ramps listed under Stages 2-1 thru 2-4 are completed. Maintain a minimum 12-foot lane width for both directions of STH 13, except the lane width may be reduced to 11-feet when adjacent to a two-way-left-turn lane as shown in the plans. Stage 2-1: Construct the pedestrian curb ramps located on the outside edges of the roadway as shown in the plans while the outside traffic lanes are closed to through traffic. Stage 2-2: Construct the pedestrian curb ramps located on the outside edges of the roadway as shown in the plans while the outside traffic lanes are closed to through traffic and after the curb ramps designated for construction in Stage 2-1 are completed and open to pedestrian traffic. Stage 2-3: Construct the pedestrian curb ramps located on the outside edges of the roadway as shown in the plans while the outside traffic lanes are closed to through traffic and after the curb ramps designated for construction in Stage 2-2 are completed and open to pedestrian traffic. Stage 2-4: Construct the pedestrian curb ramps located on the outside edges of the roadway as shown in the plans while the outside traffic lanes are closed to through traffic and after the curb ramps designated for construction in Stage 2-3 are completed and open to pedestrian traffic. Stage 3: Construct STH 13 travel lanes and shoulders from Station 1205+10 to the project ending using single lane closure with flaggers during daylight hours. Return all roads to two lanes of through traffic at the end of each workday. Stage 3 may be constructed concurrently with Stage 2, however, the requirement to construct the new overlay pavement within 48 hours after completion of the milling operations, as described under the Prosecution and Progress, still applies to the segment of STH 13 north of Station 1205+10. #### **Describe how access to traffic generators (businesses, schools, etc.) and everyday services will be maintained:**

Keep all entrances accessible at all times, except for temporary restrictions during the milling and paving operations in the immediate vicinity of the entrance. No extended closures of entrances will be allowed without approval of the engineer and written permission is obtained from the property owner 48 hours in advance of closing the access. If work is being completed on multiple driveways to the same property, conduct operations so at least one of the driveways remain open.

#### **Describe how impacts to bicycle riders will be mitigated/coordinated:**

Single lane closures will be utilized during construction. On-road bicycles may use the open lanes of traffic similar to existing conditions.

#### **Describe how impacts to railways will be mitigated/coordinated:**

The railway parallels the corridor to the west. The proposed improvements are to mill and pave up to the east side of the rail crossings. No railway impacts are anticipated.

#### **Are there anticipated traffic impacts from the proposed project on other road/routes in the region/corridor?**

Impacts to entering and exiting traffic to/from WIS 29 are anticipated during paving operations of the WIS 29 ramp intersections. Impacts will be mitigated by performing these construction operations under closed conditions during off peak night time hours. These operations are restricted to one overnight continuous closure and the ramps must be reopened to traffic within the same night that the closure began. WIS 29 traffic will be detoured to the two adjacent WIS 29 and Business 29 interchanges during the ramp closures.

#### **Does the project affect other regions/states?**

Parts of WIS 13 within the project limits run along the shared line of Marathon and Clark counties, which is also the border between the North Central and Northwest Regions. There are no conflicts in the bordering Northwest Region associated with the project.

#### **List holidays or major special events that occur during the project:**

| Holiday/Special Event      | Begin Date | End Date   |
|----------------------------|------------|------------|
| Memorial Day               | 05/26/2023 | 05/30/2023 |
| Independence Day           | 06/30/2023 | 07/05/2023 |
| Labor Day                  | 09/01/2023 | 09/05/2023 |
| Colby Cheese Days          | 07/14/2023 | 07/17/2023 |
| Abby Festival              | 06/02/2023 | 06/05/2023 |
| Abbotsford First City Days | 08/11/2023 | 08/14/2023 |

#### **How will traffic disruptions be minimized during listed events and holidays?**

No work on, nor materials of any kind hauled along or across any portion of the highway carrying WIS 13 traffic will be allowed during the aforementioned holiday periods. Also, no work on, nor materials of any kind hauled along or across any portion of the highway carrying WIS 13 traffic will be allowed within the community of Colby during the Colby Cheese Days nor within the community of Abbotsford during the Abby Festival and the Abbotsford First City Days. The traveled way and shoulders will be required to be clear of equipment, barricades, signs, lights, and any other material that might impede the free flow of traffic during the holidays and events listed.

--- End of Section 5 ---

#### **How was the work zone capacity determined?**

FDM 11-50-30 was used to determine capacity. Capacity analysis determined that the work zone capacity is 1299 pcphpl. Minimal travel delays are anticipated during construction. WIS 13 has a Directional Peak Hour Volume (DHV) of 893 vphpl through the proposed segment. DHV = AADT\*K30\*D, DHV=12500\*0.119\*0.6. The demand along WIS 13 is expected to remain under the available capacity during single lane closures.


#### **a) Are there restrictions on when lane closures are allowed?** Yes

#### **b) What hours/days are lane closures permitted?**

Lane closures are restricted during the dates and times listed in Section 5 - Work Zone Impacts, specifically in the Holiday /Special Events table.

#### **c) If the project is reporting zero delay, show the delay incurred if the lane closures hours identified are not followed:**

Traffic volumes are expected to remain under the available capacity for all hours of a typical day, therefore minimal delay is anticipated.


#### **If existing signals are impacted by the project, will there be any changes? If so, please describe any changes that will be made to the signals. If using temporary signals for one-lane two-way operations, how will the signals be timed? In either case, were pedestrian movements considered?**

The intersections at Spence Street, Adams Street, Elderberry Road, Linden Street, and Spruce Street shall remain open at all times. Traffic may be reduced to one lane on Spence Street, Adams Street, Elderberry Road, Linden Street, and Spruce Street utilizing flagging operations when construction operations are within these intersections. The STH 29 ramps may be closed between 7:00 PM and 5:00 AM Sunday through Thursday for construction. No more than two total nights of closure will be allowed. During the ramp closures, the STH 29 ramp traffic shall be detoured as shown in the plans. The ramps shall remain open to traffic at all other times during the project. Traffic access to STH 13 at all other intersections may be closed when construction operations are within the area. When an intersection is closed, adjacent intersections shall remain open to traffic.

project start date to help avoid any potential conflicts. The project special provisions prohibit full closure/detour work on STH 27 prior to June 7, 2023 to avoid impacts to school bus routes. ### **Describe how access to traffic generators (businesses, schools, etc.) and everyday services will be maintained:**

Access to all properties and side roads within the project limits will be maintained at all times throughout construction.

### **Describe how impacts to bicycle riders will be mitigated/coordinated:**

Shoulders will be closed for portions of construction. It is expected that bicycles will share the roadway with vehicles while traversing the short work zone.

### **Describe how impacts to transit users will be mitigated/coordinated:**

The existing transit route (Route 17) for Duluth Transit Authority (DTA) runs along STH 35 through the project limits. The STH 35 and STH 105 intersection has bus stops in the northwest and southeast quadrants along STH 35. These bus stop signs will be removed by DTA prior to construction and riders will be required to gain bus access at the adjacent STH 35 intersections at 60th Street and 62nd Street. Contact Rod Fournier, Director of Operations, at (218) 623-4336 within three working days of substantial completion. The northbound transit stop at the STH 35 & STH 105 intersection will be removed permanently after construction.

### **Describe how impacts to railways will be mitigated/coordinated:**

The BNSF railroad crosses the west and south legs of the project intersection. This project will not affect rail operations, but coordination efforts will take place between WisDOT and BNSF due to work activities taking place near railroad right-of-way. The contractor will be required to have a BNSF railroad flagger on site while installing the concrete medians along STH 35 and at any time while bi-directional traffic is in operations or working within 25¿ of the railroad crossing.

### **Are there anticipated traffic impacts from the proposed project on other road/routes in the region/corridor?**

There are no anticipated traffic impacts from this project on other roads/routes in the region/corridor.

This project will not affect any other regions or states.

### **How was the work zone capacity determined?**

The STH 35 & STH 105 intersection operations were analyzed using Synchro Modeling Software which has the option to emulate Highway Capacity Manual (6th Edition) methodology. Traffic models were analyzed using construction year (2020) traffic volumes for AM (7:15 AM to 8:15 AM) and PM (4:30 PM to 5:30 PM) peak hours. The eastbound approach (STH 105) is expected to operate at a LOS E during the PM peak period. Delay (35 seconds/vehicle) and queues (75-ft) are expected to remain minimal during this period. This movement currently operates at LOS E with similar delay and queue lengths. There is minor delay to STH 35 traffic due to turn lane closures. Left turning vehicles will cause mainline STH 35 traffic to slow/stop until gaps are available in the opposing direction. A Synchro traffic analysis was completed to represent flagging operations as closely as possible. It was found that queue lengths and delay increase during the AM and PM peak hours due to the flagging operations and drops to LOS E/F for all approaches. It was determined from a 48-hour coverage count (site # 160310) on STH 35 that the largest nighttime hourly traffic volume is approximately 75% less than the PM peak hour traffic volumes. This reduction was applied to the turning movement traffic volumes to determine anticipated delay and queuing impacts from the flagging operations during these nighttime hours. Delay is expected to remain minimal (less than 1 minute for all approaching vehicles to the work zone). Queue lengths are expected to increase on STH 35 due to the introduction of flagging operations stopping vehicles, but queues are not anticipated to cause any issues with STH 35 queues expected to not extend more than 150-ft . Queues are expected to remain under 50-ft in length for STH 105 and 61st Street. See Attachment D for the traffic analysis outputs.


#### **a) Are there restrictions on when lane closures are allowed?** Yes

### **b) What hours/days are lane closures permitted?**

Flagging operations are restricted to 10:00 PM to 12:00 AM and 12:00 AM to 6:00 AM. The work shall be completed in a manner which minimizes disruption to traffic.

### **c) If the project is reporting zero delay, show the delay incurred if the lane closures hours identified are not followed:**


**If existing signals are impacted by the project, will there be any changes? If so, please describe any changes that will be made to the signals. If using temporary signals for one-lane two-way operations, how will the signals be timed? In either case, were pedestrian movements considered?**

No, the work will not interfere with intersection controls. However, during the nighttime lane closures the STH 35 & STH 105 intersection will operate under flagging operations, similar to a temporary traffic signal. At the end of construction the STH 35 & STH 105 intersection will be converted to the permanent proposed traffic signal control.

--- End of Section 6 ---

#### **Describe how access to traffic generators (businesses, schools, etc.) and everyday services will be maintained:**

USH 18 will remain open to traffic throughout the project. Lane closures can be maintained 24 hours a day, except during the lane closure restriction times or holidays and events where the roadway must be opened back up. This will be necessary to limit the amount of Special High Early Strength (SHES) concrete used on the project. SHES concrete has a much higher price and lower overall service life. All lane and ramp closures are subject to the approval of the Region traffic engineer. When the work zone is not active the traffic control drums must be placed completely within the closed lane to accommodate OSOW vehicles. Access to all businesses along and near the USH 18 corridor will be maintain. There are no schools directly within the project limits. Schools near the project area are located within the Village of Mount Horeb. No impacts to schools are anticipated. Northbound STH 78 will be detoured down to the USH 18/USH 151/CTH ID interchange while work along STH 78 is completed. Southbound STH 78 will remain open at all times. CTH ID interchange will require a detour for the two EB ramps for a structure closure on the bridge work. A detour will be posted to allow for the work on the structure to allow them to complete before the ironman Wisconsin(Sept 11). Northbound CTH ID will be detoured down to the USH 18/USH 151/CTH PD interchange while work along CTH ID is completed. Southbound CTH ID will be detoured down to USH 18/USH 151/STH 78 interchange while work on structure takes place. CTH JG will be closed while the wing wall, bearings and north abutment expansion joint are replaced at B-13-300 (CTH JG over USH 18). Interim liquidated damages will be accessed if the STH 78 and CTH ID detours or the CTH JG closure exceeds the maximum calendars days shown in the special provisions. The STH 78 and CTH ID detours will not be allowed to occur at the same time. Closure of CTH JG is not permitted while the STH 78 or CTH ID detours are in place. No impacts to businesses, schools, and everyday services are anticipated while these detours or closure are in place.

Access to and crossings of the Military Ridge State Trail will be maintain at all times. Temporary pedestrian accommodations (temporary curb ramps and temporary pedestrian surfaces) shall be used as necessary to maintain access.

#### **Briefly describe the staging planned for maintaining traffic:** The existing concrete pavement along USH 18 will be concrete base patched as needed and then will be overlaid with 3.5 inches of HMA. The overlay will be placed in two lifts (both 1.75-inches) with cross slope and superelevation correction as needed. For both the lower and upper lifts, the contractor will be required to ensure pavement grades are even and pavement markings, temporary or permanent, are in place for holiday/special event openings or anytime both lanes are open to traffic. USH 18 will remain open to through traffic using the following staged construction. When the work zone is not active the traffic control drums must be placed completely within the closed lane to accommodate OSOW vehicles: Stage 1: The outside lanes of both eastbound and westbound USH 18 will be closed, with traffic utilizing the inside-median lanes, while the existing outside shoulders and rumble strips are milled and paved for Stage 2 traffic. Stage 2: The inside-median lanes of both eastbound and westbound USH 18 will be closed, with traffic utilizing both the existing outside lanes and paved outside shoulders, while the existing inside-median lanes are concrete base patched and repaired. Additional work in Stage 2 is as follows: - The inside-median shoulders and rumble strips will be milled and paved. - Inside-median intersection improvements will be made at CTH F, Cave of the Mounds & Erbe Road. - Inside-median lane approach slab and wing wall replacements where USH 18 bridges over Sand Rock Road and STH 92. Stage 3: The outside lanes of both eastbound and westbound USH 18 will be closed, with traffic utilizing both the inside-median lanes and paved inside shoulders, while the existing outside lanes are concrete base patched and repaired. Stage 3 will require a 12 foot max width restriction. Additional work in Stage 3 is as follows: - Interchange ramps at STH 78 and CTH ID are concrete based patched and repaired. Ramps will also have shoulders milled and paved. - Outside lane intersection improvements will be made at CTH F, Cave of the Mounds & Erbe Road. - Wing wall replacements for bridges B-13-299, B-13-300, and B-13-301. - Outside lane approach slab and wing wall replacements where USH 18 bridge over Sand Rock Road and STH 92. Stage 4: The outside lanes of both eastbound and westbound USH 18 will remain closed, with traffic utilizing both the inside-median lanes and paved inside shoulders, while the existing outside lanes and shoulders are overlaid with the lower layer. Stage 4 will require a 12 foot max width restriction. Additional work in Stage 4 is as follows: - Crown and superelevation correction will be made with lower layer. - Interchange ramps and shoulders at STH 78 and CTH ID will be overlaid with lower layer. Stage 5: The inside-median lanes of both eastbound and westbound USH 18 will be closed, with traffic utilizing both the overlaid outside lanes and shoulders, while the inside-median lanes and shoulders are overlaid with the lower and upper layer. Stage 6: The outside lanes of both eastbound and westbound USH 18 will remain closed, with traffic utilizing both the overlaid inside-median lanes and paved inside shoulders, while the outside lanes and shoulders are overlaid with the upper layer. Stage 6 will require a 12 foot max width restriction. Additional work in Stage 6 is as follows: - Interchange ramps and shoulders at STH 78 and CTH ID will be overlaid with upper layer. - Outside lane intersection improvements at CTH F, Cave of the Mounds & Erbe Road will have upper layer paved. - Outside guardrail will be replaced as necessary - Outside shoulder will be graveled - Minor outside slope grading. - Outside rumble strips installed - Outside lane and centerline pavement markings installed. Stage 7: The inside-median lanes of both eastbound and westbound USH 18 will be closed, with traffic utilizing both the overlaid outside lanes and shoulders, while the inside-median lane rumble strips and pavement marking is installed. NB STH 78 Detour: NB STH 78 will be detoured while the existing concrete is removed and replaced with 6.5-inches of HMA from CTH E to CTH ID and the approach slabs on STH 78 are replaced. SB STH 78 will remain open at all times. NB STH 78 traffic will be detoured to the CTH ID interchange and will follow CTH ID until reaching STH 78. This same detour route is used for STH 92. #### **How was the work zone capacity determined?**

STH 32 has a 2017 AADT of 13,000. The WisDOT planning-level forecasts do not show any traffic growth at this location, so for the purpose of this analysis a 2% annual growth rate was used. The construction year (2021) AADT would be approximately 14,000. This corridor has a Seasonal Factor Group (SFG) 2 for Urban Other. This results in a K30 value of 0.12 and a directional distribution of 59/41. The peak hour directional volume along STH 32 is estimated to be 990 vph. There is not expected to be any capacity issues along this portion of STH 32 since capacity of a single lane is expected to be higher than 1,000 vphpl. Capacity will be reduced even further at the STH 32 & STH 11 intersection due to closing one lane of the EB left turn movement and one NB thru lane. Synchro 11 and SimTraffic traffic modeling software, using Highway Capacity Manual (HCM) 6th Edition methodology, was used to estimate traffic conditions during these closures. Traffic Volumes were estimated based on AADTs on each leg of the intersection. - STH 11: 2017 AADT of 9,600 - STH 32 (South of STH 11): 2017 AADT 11,600 - STH 32 (North of STH 11): 2017 AADT 13,000 These AADTs were converted into K30 directional volumes based on a K30 value of 0.12 and an assume directional distribution of 50/50. Turning movement volumes were proportioned out based on the demand on each leg of the intersection and projected to year 2021 volumes using a 2% annual growth rate. It was determined that the intersection will remain under capacity. There will be minor delay due to these lane closures and queue lengths are not expected to be an issue. Traffic volumes are likely to still be low due to COVID impacts in the summer of 2021, which will assist in keeping STH 32 well under capacity. See Attachment 3 for the traffic analysis outputs.

### **Describe how access to traffic generators (businesses, schools, etc.) and everyday services will be maintained:**

The Fahey Glen portion of the project is a new roadway. Services will not be disrupted for access at this location. Access for East Cheryl Parkway will be rerouted to other local routes for the duration of construction. Alternate routes will add less than 5 minutes onto any travel time.

### **Describe how impacts to bicycle riders will be mitigated/coordinated:**

The project will close the existing path running along the south side of East Cheryl during the construction. Bike and pedestrians will need to find alternate routes via parallel route including Lacy Route. A specific bike/ped detour will not be provided.

### **Describe how impacts to transit users will be mitigated/coordinated:**

Madison Metro Transit has one route along East Cheryl Parkway. The route operates in the AM and PM hours with 5 trips at a frequency of every 30 minutes during this duration. Construction flaggers will allow transit passage through the work zone during route hours by way of gravel surface.

### **Are there anticipated traffic impacts from the proposed project on other road/routes in the region/corridor?**

Lacy Road is a parallel route. Due to the closure of East Cheryl Parkway, Lacy Road will likely see a slight increase in traffic.

No

#### **Describe how access to traffic generators (businesses, schools, etc.) and everyday services will be maintained:**

USH 18 will remain open to traffic throughout the project. Lane closures can be maintained 24 hours a day. All lane closures are subject to the approval of the Region traffic engineer. Access to all business along and near the USH 18 corridor will be maintain. There are no schools directly within the project limits. Schools near the project area are located within the Village of Mount Horeb, Village of Barneveld, and Village of Ridgeway. No impacts to schools are anticipated. Access to everyday services will be maintain throughout the duration of the project.

#### **Are there anticipated traffic impacts from the proposed project on other road/routes in the region/corridor?**

There are no anticipated traffic impacts.

#### **Does the project affect other regions/states?**

This project is not anticipated to affect other regions/states.

| Labor Day (09/06/2021)             | 09/03/2021 | 09/07/2021 |
| Good Friday/Easter                 | 04/02/2021 | 04/05/2021 |
| Opening Weekend of Gun Deer Season | 11/19/2021 | 11/22/2021 |

#### **How will traffic disruptions be minimized during listed events and holidays?**

All closures will not be allowed during University of Wisconsin home football games and for 4 hours before and 4 hours after the game (contractor to verify schedule). The Village of Mount Horeb, Village of Barneveld, and Village of Ridgeway hold numerous annual events from May to October. It is not anticipated that there will be much congestion for these events as there are many alternative routes in and out of the Villages. Traffic control must be taken down/moved to the shoulder for holidays, University of Wisconsin home football games, and special events. All lane closures are subject to the approval of the Region traffic engineer.

STH 29 will be closed to local traffic at the C-47-0719 culvert during replacement, but traffic may bypass this closure by utilizing local roads as an alternate route or the proposed signed detour.

The multi-use path along STH 29 will be closed between the CTH FF and Cemetery Road intersections due to the box culvert construction near the 805th Avenue intersection. A pedestrian/bicycle detour will be provided in this area. This proposed detour route requires an additinoal 0.3 miles of travel distance for all pedestrians and bicycles. See Attachment C for the pedestrian/bicycle detour plan. The multi-use path will be reconstructed in the SE quadrant of the STH 29 & Cemetery Road intersection. Since there is no continuous sidewalk on the north side of STH 29/ 830th Ave, bicycles will be required to find an alternate route using local roads for this short period. All other portions of the multi-use trail will remain open during construction.

Minimal traffic impacts are expected along USH 10 and STH 65 due to the proposed detour route.

### **Brief description of work activities:**

Project ID 7650-00-04/74: The spot improvement project consists of replacing Culvert C-47-719 under STH 29 just south of 805th Avenue with a two-cell concrete box culvert B-47-0230. Due to the depth of the culvert, it is required to reconstruct the roadway for approximately 70' feet north and south of the culvert, install new guardrail along both sides of the roadway, and reconstruct the multi-use trail along the east side of the roadway. The existing safety rail along the multi-use trail will be salvaged and replaced. The reconstructed roadway will include a 7-inch asphaltic pavement over base aggregate and will maintain 12-foot travel lanes but will provide a wider 5-foot paved shoulder and 3-foot gravel shoulder. Centerline and shoulder rumble strips will be constructed. All new pavement marking will be installed as well. Project ID 7650-01-05/75: The pavement replacement project along STH 29 includes replacing the existing 7-inch concrete pavement with new 7-inch asphaltic pavement. The 12-foot travel lanes will be maintained, as well as the overall shoulder width of 8 feet; however, the paved shoulder will be widened to 5 feet. Both the roadway cross slope and the superelevation of the curve just south of the STH 29 and 690th Street intersection will be adjusted to current design standards. The existing bypass lane for westbound

STH 29 traffic at CTH E will be removed and a dedicated left turn lane will be provided. The curb and gutter in the southeast quadrant of the STH 29 and Cemetery Road intersection will be redesigned to accommodate large truck turning movements. Centerline and shoulder rumble strips will be constructed. One culvert along the project limits will be replaced and another two culverts will be extended; all other existing culverts will remain. All existing guardrail within the project limits will be replaced. All new pavement marking will be installed as well. The project also includes rehabilitating the bridge B-47-21 over Greenwood Valley Creek. The top 1.5 inches of the existing bridge deck will be removed and replaced with a new 1.5-inch concrete surface. The bridge deck will be widened 8 inches and new, crash-worthy bridge railing will be installed. Guardrail will be replaced in all quadrants of the bridge approach. New concrete pavement approach slabs will be constructed north and south of the existing bridge. All rebar that has been exposed will be properly cleaned and sealed to maintain its structural integrity. Maintenance of the superstructure will be completed. Project ID 7650-02-03/73: The HSIP project includes reconfiguring the STH 29 and CTH FF intersection to provide dedicated left turn lanes for westbound and eastbound STH 29 traffic, a dedicated right turn lane for westbound STH 29 traffic, and reconfiguring the channelized right turn lane on the west leg of County FF. To reduce impacts to the multi-use trail and adjacent properties, the east side of the roadway edge will be maintained and widening of STH 29 will occur to the west. One existing culvert south of CTH FF will be extended. Shoulder rumble strips will be constructed. All new signs and pavement marking will be installed as well. See Attachment A for the project location maps.

The K30 directional volume is equal to 430 vphpl in 2021, based on the previous traffic forecast's design values.STH 29 is expected to remain under capacity throughout all of construction. The introduction of flagging operations during construction is expected to introduce minimal delay since these work zone limits will be quite short for the asphalt patching operations. The introduction of flagging operations during Stage 2 of construction, between the 950th Street roundabout and the STH 65 roundabout, is expected to introduce 1.5 minutes of delay per vehicle (Analysis was only completed for STH 29 traffic and operations could potentially worsen depending on the volume entering at 950th Street) during peak hours and the expected queues reach 500'-750' during those peak hours. STH 29 is expected to operate at a LOS F during flagging operations at peak hour periods. If queuing become an issue at the STH 29 & STH 65 intersection then flaggers will have to prioritize demand to assure queuing remains on STH 29 and does not extend back onto STH 65. Note that these operations may potentially not get this severe as traffic will divert to other routes if congestion becomes an issue. Stage 2 of construction is expected to last approximately 7 days. The STH 29 & Cemetery Road intersection will be under construction for a period of time. The signal will need to be deenergized during construction. The signal will be controlled by the folding stop-signs during this period. This work is only anticipated to take 2-5 working days to complete. ## **Briefly describe the staging planned for maintaining traffic:** Maintain access to properties within the work zone. Driveway access may be closed for the minimum time required for milling and mainline paving operations through the driveway. Provide a minimum 48-hour notice of access closure. Maintain access to side roads for emergency vehicles and buses. Stage 1 Traffic will be on the existing WB lane and two-way left turn lane from Sta. 587+90 to Sta. 637+75 except for a lane shift between Sta. 588+75 and Sta. 591+50. Use daytime flagging for construction within the roundabout if needed. Stage 2 Traffic will be on the existing WB lane and two-way left turn lane from Sta. 587+90 to Sta. 637+75. Use daytime flagging for construction within the roundabout and from Sta. 637+75 to Sta. 652+50. Use traffic control for moving operations during installation of permanent pavement markings. Stage 3 Traffic will be on the existing WB lane and two-way left turn lane from Sta. 587+90 to Sta. 637+75. Use daytime flagging for milling and paving through intersections if needed. Stage 4 Traffic will be on the new EB lane and existing two-way left turn lane from Sta. 587+90 to Sta. 637+75. Use daytime flagging for milling and paving through intersections if needed. Stage 5 Traffic will be on the new EB and WB lanes from Sta. 587+90 to Sta. 637+75. Use daytime flagging for milling and paving through intersections if needed. Use traffic control for moving operations during installation of permanent pavement markings. See Attachment E for the traffic control staging plans. #### **Describe how pedestrians will be accommodated during construction.** All pedestrian curb ramps will be constructed in stage 1, excluding 6th Street curb ramps to be constructed in Stage 4. While curb ramps are being upgraded in Stage 1 and Stage 4, pedestrians will be accommodated with temporary pedestrian curb ramps and surface. #### **Describe how access to traffic generators (businesses, schools, etc.) and everyday services will be maintained:**

I-94 will remain open to traffic throughout construction with two-lanes in each direction during daytime hours (except to accommodate daytime cable barrier work - see TMP ID 7551) and a minimum of one-lane in each direction during overnight hours (as identified in Section 6). Interchange ramps to/from I-94 located within the project limits will remain open to traffic during daytime hours. Overnight ramp closures (3 to 4 total nights per location) are required to accommodate milling and paving operations on the ramps. Signed detours will be not be provided for the ramp closures. Current correspondence with impacted groups includes the minutes from the December 2018 Public Involvement Meeting, which are attached in this section.

### **Describe how impacts to transit users will be mitigated/coordinated:**

Several long distance intercity bus lines (Badger Bus, Greyhound, Megabus, Lamers) utilize this section of I-94. The roadway will remain open to traffic throughout the project. No impacts to the intercity long distance bus service are expected due to construction.

#### **Are there anticipated traffic impacts from the proposed project on other road/routes in the region/corridor?**

The majority of traffic is expected to continue using I-94 during construction (for analysis purposes, no diversion was assumed). The roadway will remain open to traffic throughout the project with two-lanes in each direction during daytime hours (except to accommodate daytime cable barrier work - see TMP ID 7551) and a minimum of one-lane in each direction during overnight hours (as identified in Section 6). Ramp closures are limited to overnight hours only, when traffic volumes are low. Therefore, no traffic impacts are anticipated on other roads/routes in the area.

### **Does the project affect other regions/states?**

The eastern project limits fall on the Jefferson/Waukesha County line, which is also the boarder between WisDOT Southwest Region (Jefferson County) and Southeast Region (Waukesha County). Mainline traffic control associated with the overnight lane closures will extend into the Southeast Region, but all construction activities will remain in the Southwest Region. Coordination with Southeast Region is ongoing and will continue throughout construction. The project does not affect another state.

### **List holidays or major special events that occur during the project:**

| Holiday/Special Event                    | Begin Date | End Date   |
|------------------------------------------|------------|------------|
| Memorial Day                             | 05/28/2021 | 06/01/2021 |
| Independence Day                         | 07/02/2021 | 07/06/2021 |
| Labor Day                                | 09/03/2021 | 09/07/2021 |
| Thanksgiving                             | 11/24/2021 | 11/29/2021 |
| Wisconsin Badger Home Football Game Days | 09/01/2021 | 12/11/2021 |
| Milwaukee Brewers Home Game Days         | 03/01/2021 | 11/15/2021 |

#### **How will traffic disruptions be minimized during listed events and holidays?**

No roadway work, lane closures, or hauling of materials will be allowed during the time periods listed above. Westbound lane closures are not permitted starting four hours prior to kickoff of a home game for the Wisconsin Badgers football team, concluding at kickoff. Eastbound lane closures are not permitted starting at half time of a home game for the Wisconsin Badgers football team, concluding six hours after completion of the game. Eastbound lane closures are not permitted starting three hours prior to start of a home game for the Milwaukee Brewers, concluding at the start of the game. Westbound lane closures are not permitted starting at the seventh inning of a home game for the Milwaukee Brewers, concluding three hours after the completion of the game.

### **Briefly describe the staging planned for maintaining traffic:** Mainline I-94 will remain open to traffic throughout the project and work will be completed under staged construction. Staging plans are attached in this section. Single lane closures (reduced from 2-lanes to 1-lane) are permitted in each direction during overnight hours only (permitted closure times are identified in Section 6). The majority of work including pavement milling, base patching, and repaving operations will occur during the overnight hours when the lane closures are in place. Work not requiring lane closures may occur during daytime hours. See TMP ID 7551 for limited permitted daytime lane closure hours associated with the cable barrier work. Schedule/Sequencing of work and traffic control will be coordinated between the three tied let projects. Construction will include two general stages to avoid traffic control conflicts between the railroad bridge rehab and resurfacing projects (see description below). The cable barrier Segment 1 project is located within the resurfacing project limits and will be installed concurrently with the resurfacing work. Traffic control staging must be coordinated between these two projects. During overnight work, either separate work zones must be established for the cable barrier and resurfacing work with a minimum separation of 3 miles or a single work zone must be established encompassing both work activities that may not exceed 5 miles in length. Further, an inside lane closure for cable barrier work may not be preceded or followed by an outside lane closure for resurfacing work. The cable barrier Segment 2 limits are located more than 3 miles away from the CNW Railroad bridges (1067-01-85) and the resurfacing (1067-04-72) projects, allowing for separate work zone operations. However, the cable barrier Segment 2 is located in close proximity (less than 1 mile east) of a bridge re-decking/widening project along the County A overpass of I-94 (1067-02-72) which is scheduled to occur simultaneously in 2021. Overnight lane closures along I-94 are proposed with the County A overpass project. Due to the proximity of the work zones, lane closures with the cable barrier Segment 2 and County A overpass projects must be coordinated and any lane closures occurring simultaneously must be implemented to provide a single, continuous work zone. Overall project sequencing is summarized below. \*Stage 1 (May-July, 2021): -Complete westbound bridge rehab work. - Complete eastbound road resurfacing work. -Westbound road resurfacing work may occur with a minimum 3-mile separation maintained between the westbound bridge work. -Complete cable barrier Segment 1. Coordinate traffic control with resurfacing work (as discussed in previous paragraphs). -Complete cable barrier Segment 2. #### **Describe how access to traffic generators (businesses, schools, etc.) and everyday services will be maintained:**

Access to traffic generators will be maintained throughout construction. The milling and paving operations along mainline STH 172 will be completed under traffic. Single lane closures will be permitted in both directions. A full closure will be required to complete the work along the single lane STH 172/IH 41 interchange ramps. Traffic will be detoured for the WB STH 172 ramp to SB IH 41 while the concrete pavement is being replaced. The detour will direct traffic along NB IH 41 to CTH VK (Lombardi Avenue). The work for the other single lane ramps will not have detours but lane closures will be allowed as specified in the lane closures.

#### **Describe how impacts to bicycle riders will be mitigated/coordinated:**

The curb ramps at the STH 172 & Packerland Drive/CTH EB and the STH 172 & Babcock Road intersections will be replaced with the project. While the curb ramps are being replaced the associated Packerland Drive bike trail will be closed and appropriate signage will be in place (see attached Traffic Control Plan). The public will be informed of the planned work and closure of the path through public involvement meetings, press releases/media alerts, the project website, and through the 511 Traveler Information Website.

#### **Describe how impacts to airports will be mitigated/coordinated:**

Airport personnel will be notified of the project and will be kept informed of changes in traffic control during construction by construction personnel. Lane closures will only be allowed during the times specified in the special provisions. The public will be informed of the planned work and lane closures through public involvement meetings, press releases/media alerts, the project website, and through the 511 Traveler Information Website.

#### **Are there anticipated traffic impacts from the proposed project on other road/routes in the region/corridor?**

IH 41 and CTH VK (Lombardi Avenue) traffic will be impacted by the project. Traffic along the WB STH 172 ramp to SB IH 41 will be detoured along NB IH 41 to CTH VK while the concrete pavement along the ramp is being replaced. The detour route will be signed per the traffic control plans.

#### **Does the project affect other regions/states?**

No.

#### **How will traffic disruptions be minimized during listed events and holidays?**

The special provisions will include language indicating, "Do not perform work on, nor haul materials of any kind along or across any portion of the highway carrying STH 172 traffic and entirely clear the traveled way and shoulders of such portions of the highway of equipment, barricades, signs, lights, and any other material that might impede the free flow of traffic during the events listed above".

#### **Briefly describe the staging planned for maintaining traffic:** The milling and paving operations along mainline STH 172 will be completed under traffic. Single lane closures will be permitted in both directions. The maintenance crossover west of IH 41 will be closed off using type III barricades to prevent drivers from utilizing them during the STH 172/IH 41 ramp closures. A full closure will be required to complete the work along the single lane STH 172/IH 41 interchange ramps. Traffic will be detoured for the WB STH 172 ramp to SB IH 41 while the concrete pavement is being replaced. The detour will direct traffic along NB IH 41 to CTH VK (Lombardi Avenue). The work for the other single lane ramps will not have detours but lane closures will not be allowed between 6:00 am and 6:00 pm. #### **Describe how pedestrians will be accommodated during construction.** The curb ramps at the STH 172 & Packerland Drive/CTH EB intersection and STH 172/Babcock Road intersection will be replaced with the project. While the curb ramps are being replaced the associated sidewalk will be closed and appropriate signage will be in place. The public will be informed of the planned work and closure of the sidewalk through notifications to locals, press releases/media alerts, and through the 511 Traveler Information Website. The plan is to reach out to providers in the area prior to the closures that can help with transportation. This includes the ADRC, for people with disabilities, and local taxi service, for any other pedestrians. Notifications will be sent out to local municipalities, providers, and a press release about the closure and transportation options. This will get the word out about this work and get users to think ahead. The ADRC has a list of providers. Most are on-demand services. They can provide rides for all kinds of reasons. It is very possible that people with disabilities using these corridors have used these services before to get around town. People can call them directly and discuss transportation. If they use the route daily, then the transportation can be catered to their needs. This will depend on individual needs. As previously discussed, construction of these ramps will occur early in the spring when weather is not ideal, so it's anticipated less pedestrians are utilizing the walks. FMS will be placed at closure points to catch the pedestrians that did not see the notifications. It will provide phone numbers for the services. Temporary curb ramps with cross walks were investigated at the intersections. Due to the geometry of the existing intersection with raised medians, a signalized intersection, and a 4 lane facility with higher speeds on STH 172, temporary crosswalk accommodations could not safely be provided. A detour of the sidewalk was investigated at each intersection. Due to the more rural nature of the intersections, the shortest detour route would be 1.2 miles in length. It was decided a detour would not be provided. A shuttle service was contacted to provide accommodations at the intersections. #### **Describe how access to traffic generators (businesses, schools, etc.) and everyday services will be maintained:**

Parking is currently not allowed along USH 14. Access will be maintained to businesses during construction. Driveway access will be maintained by constructing driveways half at a time or if there are multiple driveways present then access to at least one driveway will be maintained. Key intersections at 13th Street and 15th Street will be gapped to allow continuous access.

#### **Describe how impacts to bicycle riders will be mitigated/coordinated:**

There are no existing or proposed separate bicycle facilities along USH 14. Bicyclists looking to cross USH 14 during construction will utilize the same crossing locations at side streets shown as on the traffic control and pedestrian access plan.

#### **Describe how impacts to transit users will be mitigated/coordinated:**

Existing bus stops will be maintained as much as possible during construction; however, they will need to be temporarily closed/relocated at some point during construction. See the pedestrian access plan for more information. Coordination with La Crosse MTU to discuss stop locations, bus schedules, and the need for temporary or relocated bus stops during construction has been completed during four meetings held on 8/12/20, 9/16/20, 10/20/20, and 12/9/20.

#### **Describe how impacts to railways will be mitigated/coordinated:**

Coordination with the BSNF Railroad to determine if they will do any work on the crossing as part of the project has been been provided to BSNF and is in the process of being finalized. The crossings at South Avenue, West Avenue, and Barlow Street will be maintained during construction. See the traffic control plan for more information.

#### **Are there anticipated traffic impacts from the proposed project on other road/routes in the region/corridor?**

It is anticipated that motorists may divert to other routes to avoid the construction zone. Impacted routes may include Losey Blvd, 16th Street, and STH 33.

#### **Does the project affect other regions/states?**

N/A

| Labor Day             | 09/01/2023 | 09/05/2023 |

## **How will traffic disruptions be minimized during listed events and holidays?**

During these times, no work will be performed, and no materials of any kind will be hauled along or across any portion of the highway carrying USH 14 traffic, and the traveled way of the highway will be entirely cleared of equipment, barricades, signs, lights, and any other material that might impede the free flow of traffic.

#### **Describe how access to traffic generators (businesses, schools, etc.) and everyday services will be maintained:**

All access to commercial and private entrances will be maintained during construction. During the construction of B-55-0288, USH 12 will be closed to through traffic and all through traffic will utilize a detour route. All local traffic will be required to utilize other local roads to get around the closure and access properties. In addition, during the closure the reconstruction between Wolf Street and Broadway Street (1 block) will be completed. All local traffic will be required to utilize adjacent local roads to get around the closure, but access to properties within the reconstruct limits will be maintained as much as feasible.

#### **Are there anticipated traffic impacts from the proposed project on other road/routes in the region/corridor?**

During the detour of USH 12, traffic will be diverted. The official detour will utilize STH 65 to IH 94 to USH 63. Being that the route only utilizes state, interstate, and US highways, no additional improvements will be necessary along the detour route and these highways should be able to accommodate large trucks and carry the additional traffic and truck loadings. It is anticipated that local traffic may utilize other alternative routes in the area using county and local roads to minimize travel delay during the closure.

#### **Does the project affect other regions/states?**

No, this project will not have affect on other regions/states.
